# Tenant memo: Wicker Park, Chicago

saved example from 2026-10-15. Aggregates only. This file stores no Qloo response. Scores and overlap are stated for the example. Rent ceilings are the City Scan model for the example point. The certificate, the rent split and the pop-up line are computed from those figures. The point is an example on the map, not a vetted address.

## Recommendation
Ramen shop leads this example (GO, score 78).

## Shortlist
- **Ramen shop**: GO, stated score 78, example rank 1 of 3. Rent: Asking rent 2600 is within the ceiling 3230.
- **Chicken sandwich**: ADJUST, stated score 58, example rank 2 of 3. Rent: Asking rent 2600 is within the ceiling 2790.
- **Grain bowl**: NO-GO, stated score 36, example rank 3 of 3. Rent: Asking rent 2600 is within the ceiling 3230.

## Limits
- Qloo describes aggregate taste affinities of an area's audience, not foot traffic, sales or any individual.
- Demand scores in this saved example are stated aggregates, not a Qloo rank call, and are not absolute.
- White space comes from OpenStreetMap venues near the unit where the city has a venue file (mapping is incomplete), else from the places Qloo returns inside the area (capped at 10); neither is a census of competitors.
- Rent ceilings are a survival model built from official data, not a forecast; cafés are not covered.
- Score breakdowns split TasteFit's own scoring model (stated weights), not cause and effect; the check values come from TasteFit's stated cost assumptions, not your figures.
- The unit is a point on a map, not a vetted address.
- Demand already there: West Town had 6.3% of Chicago evening rideshare drop-offs (2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, dataset m6dm-c72p) and 6.3% of weekend drop-offs, 6.9% of Divvy trip ends (2019-01-01 to 2019-12-31, dataset fg6s-gzvg), and 3.6% of CTA 'L' station entries (2022-01-01 to 2022-12-31, dataset 5neh-572f). Community-area totals from the City of Chicago Data Portal, not a count at this door, and not a vetted address. In the Chicago backtest, footfall did not beat a citywide baseline.
- Test before you lease: a 8-week pop-up for Ramen shop. Success is your real covers per day (door counts at a comparable venue) at least 70.0 covers/day, the mode break-even at the rent-first ceiling of 3230 USD/month. The top of the ceiling's 90% range would move that line to 71.5 covers/day. From TasteFit's stated cost assumptions, not your figures. Monthly figures, no interest and no discounting. Trial plan `82839e1cada1151ca159c1ea3e0d8013c52376f6b36d1f542ea0dc92894488cc`. When the pop-up ends, log the observed value, the weeks run and whether it cleared. That log is not the five-field prediction fingerprint. A pop-up is not a vetted address.
- In a Chicago backtest of 2023-2024 openings, neither Qloo demand rankings nor the Taste Gap Index predicted which concepts opened and survived better than a citywide baseline: read them as taste and supply evidence, not a survival forecast.
